newsitem.title: UK: Northern bemoans impact of beef crisis.
newsitem.headline: Northern bemoans impact of beef crisis.

text.p: Sir Christopher Haskins, chairman of British food producer Northern Foods, said on Wednesday the impact of the beef crisis on food manufacturing and processing had been seriously under estimated.
"We have seen a significant swing in our products offered to M&S (Marks and Spencer Plc). 33 of our 35 new lines will have no beef in them," Haskins told reporters.
He said total consumption of beef was off 20 to 30 percent since fears first surfaced over the likely link between BSW, or mad-cow disease, and a similar brain wasting disease in humans.
Sales of minced beef, including packaged foods like lasagne, are off as much as 50 percent.
"We have seen no material recovery in consumer demand for beef, we would be glad if it stabilised," said Haskins.

Earlier the company reported sales of its meat products were off 6.8 percent in the six months ended September 30 as shoppers continued to worry about mad-cow disease. The company estimated the beef crisis cost it about 3.0 million stg in the first half.
Profits from its dairy business were off 27 percent at 21.6 million stg in the first half, hit by weak commodity prices for its butter, cream and milk powder.
The company took a 91 million stg charge in 1995 for re-shaping its dairy business, a move which resulted in staff cuts of about 3,300.

"I do not think there is more pain coming in our dairy business. We have finished taking pain there," said Haskins. "I think there is too much capacity in the dairy industry and excess costs of 75 to 100 million pounds.".
"I think there will be a shake-out at some time. Some people are waiting to see if a cut in milk prices will be a salvation but I still think the industry will need to rationalise," he added.

A pint of milk in supermarkets costs about 28p, 10p cheaper than one delivered to the doorstep. Competition to supply the main supermarkets remains fierce, forcing some of the smaller, regional dairies out of business.
